endorsements.quote: Participants must be made aware of risk factors, including the specific biomarkers that could be inferred from their data, the ways in which this information might be used, the irreversibility of model training, the limited control over external AI systems, and the high level of uncertainty about future LLM capabilities.
To solve this problem, greater institutional emphasis should be placed on privacy-aware data processing before public release instead of post hoc regulation of LLM research.

unlisted_practices: Obtain informed opt-in consent that explicitly covers LLM and AI use of biosignals data at the point of data collection.
Digitize consent processes and link them directly to data repositories so participants can update or withdraw consent.
Train research teams on LLM applications and risks, including simulation training, so they can inform participants accurately.
Develop anonymization methods for biosignals, such as voice de-identification, and apply them before public data release.
Make public biosignals datasets available for LLM research and avoid data use agreements that excessively restrict LLM and API use.
Conduct clinical biosignals LLM studies using the tools already used by clinicians and patients.
Institutions should carry out data security risk assessments and regulatory processes before public data release and adopt standardized data management guidelines across institutions.
Do not hold individual researchers liable for institutional data breaches; allocate liability according to controllable factors and share responsibility between researchers and institutions.
Develop a biosignals data repository adhering to FAIR principles.

screen.reason: Commentary presenting recommendations on public biosignal data sharing and governance to ethically facilitate LLM research.
